label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: deciding source logs PARTIAL; durable backlog peak 579

A.rule: throughput shortfall without a slow consumer component

report.summary: Outbox publications stalled while transfers kept arriving, so notifications are delayed. Delivery logs and timings are missing, so the cause of the stall is not identified.

findings.claim: Outbox publication stopped at about 03:49:10 and resumed only near the end of the window, while arrivals continued at 30-38 per 10 s.
findings.reason: Publications fell from ~31 per bucket to 0 for about 17 buckets; 469 of 760 arrivals went unpublished.

findings.claim: The backlog is growing and the oldest undelivered item is about 10 hours old; failed count rose from 296 to 433.
findings.reason: Pending rose from 3 to a max of 459, oldest age is ~36,500 s, and failed grew during the window.

findings.claim: The transfer API and DB pool were healthy, so the delay is in outbox delivery, not request handling or pool exhaustion.
findings.reason: All 760 requests returned 201 with p99 0.25 s; pool had 0 timeouts and 0 pending borrowers.

limitations: Delivery logs and timings are PARTIAL with 0 records, so there is no per-attempt outcome or error type.
Blocker sampling was UNAVAILABLE (0/120 samples), and the build is a dirty revision.
E3 (search_delivery_logs) is PARTIAL: The collector has not yet confirmed reading the ledgercore log past the window end; recent records may be missing.
E4 (get_delivery_timings) is PARTIAL: The collector has not yet confirmed reading the ledgercore log past the window end; recent records may be missing.
E6 (get_database_blockers) is UNAVAILABLE: Blocking is sampled every 2 s: shorter blocks can be missed, and no blocking in the samples is not proof that no session waited.
next_checks: Re-collect the ledgercore delivery logs once the collector has read past the window end, and check attempt outcomes for 03:49-03:52.
Check the consumer at 127.0.0.1:18090/events for errors, auth failures or latency, and look for DB blocking during the stall.

alternatives.reason: Rising failed count fits this, but no attempt logs or consumer timings exist to confirm it.
alternatives.hypothesis: Consumer endpoint 127.0.0.1:18090/events is failing or slow, causing delivery failures and retries.

alternatives.reason: Blocker sampling was unavailable for the whole window, so blocking can be neither shown nor ruled out.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database lock or blocker is stalling the outbox poller.
